meta.title: x/tools/gopls: "expected declaration, found 'package'" after cutting and pasting a file's contents
meta.fix_ref: golang/tools@77f530d86f9a (internal/lsp: handle deletion of file content; CL 243577, 'Fixes golang/go#38424')
meta.build_notes: Both built with the local Go (go1.27.1) through a wrapper module (their go.mod replaces x/tools); the server runs the local go command. v0.4.3 was tagged 2020-07-08, the fix merged 2020-07-21, v0.4.4 was tagged 2020-07-29.
meta.notes: The server treated a change whose resulting content is empty like a change without content and kept the previous overlay text, so after cutting a file's whole content its view of the buffer diverged from the client's; the next paste was applied to the stale text. The fix distinguishes empty content from missing content (only a save may come without content).

files.note: the go.mod of the fix's regression test TestCutAndPaste (internal/lsp/regtest/diagnostics_test.go at 77f530d8); the issue gives no code
the file main2.go of the fix's regression test TestCutAndPaste (a second file of package main)
empty, as the buffer TestCutAndPaste creates and saves (CreateBuffer("main.go", "") then a save)

repro.steps: The fix's regression test TestCutAndPaste, which reproduces the issue: open the empty main.go and save it; type 'package main' with an empty func main and save; cut the whole content (delete lines 0-4); paste a new content with 'var x int' in main. Reported: the error "expected declaration, found 'package'" (the server's copy of the buffer still holds the cut text); expected: only the unused-variable error on x. Probe: the diagnostics of main.go after the edits are compared with a fresh session on the final text and a fresh control.
